title: speculative-local-proxies-and-exec-resume-prd-draft
content:
Overview:

This PRD explores a developer-centered approach for making hosted API tool calls and streaming responses robust in flaky networks and low-connectivity environments. The core idea is a lightweight SDK pattern that allows clients to speculatively execute a small, deterministic local proxy (a "local-proxy stub") for common tool interactions, continue rendering progressive results, and then reconcile with the canonical server-side execution once connectivity is restored.

Why this exists (problem statement):
- Mobile and embedded clients experience intermittent connectivity and high tail latency; developers want smooth UX for tool-assisted flows (search, calendar writes, code execution).
- Current streaming flows either block on server-side tool resolution or force coarse-grained fallbacks that lose structure (JSON blobs) or developer intent.
- Reconciliation of tool results across partial local results and later server canonical outputs is brittle today.

Goals (success metrics):
- Reduce user-visible tool-latency by 30% in median for target mobile workloads via speculative local-proxies.
- Keep divergence rate (local proxy result differing from canonical server result) < 5% for curated set of deterministic tools (lookup, simple calc, contact lookup).
- Provide clear SDK primitives for: start speculative execution, attach progressive stream, mark reconciliation points, and accept/reject server canonical replacement.
- Instrumentation: per-request reconciliation events visible in Console and per-route cost/latency telemetry.

Non-goals:
- Not attempting to support arbitrary remote side-effects locally (no speculative writes to external systems without explicit durable confirmation).
- Not solving large-model state divergence; focus is on small deterministic tool stubs and prefix-level streaming UX.

Proposed surface and developer flows:
1) Invocation model (REST + SDK ergonomic sugar):
- /v1/resumable-invoke (POST) takes: prompt, tool-contracts (schema refs), resume_token optional.
- SDK: client.invokeSpeculative(prompt, {tools: [ToolSpec..], onPartial: cb}) returns a stream handle.

2) Local-proxy stub model:
- ToolSpec includes: id, deterministic-hint (boolean), local-stub-code (optional small WASM or JS snippet), schema for output.
- By default we ship curated stubs for common tools (calendar.lookup, contact.resolve, simple-math). Customers can opt-in additional stubs.
- SDK executes the stub synchronously to produce a speculative frame that is immediately emitted on the streaming channel as "speculative: true".

3) Streaming semantics and reconciliation frames:
- Stream frames carry metadata: frame_id, speculative(boolean), seq, schema_version, reconciliation_anchor(optional).
- When server canonical result arrives it sends a reconciliation frame: {frame_id, canonical: true, resolved_output, diff_patch(optional)}.
- SDK exposes callback onReconcile(frame_id, canonical_output, acceptCallback). Default behavior: accept server canonical and replace speculative frames in UI with smooth transition. App can call acceptCallback(false) to keep local UX and emit conflict event.

4) Structured output and schema negotiation:
- We use compact schema refs (semantic id strings) instead of full JSON schemas on the wire. The SDK caches schemas and falls back to lightweight validation.
- Partial frames may provide partial-JSON compatible fragments; we define a reconciliation patch format limited to JSON Patch operations (RFC6902 subset) to keep diffs small.

SDK ergonomics and migration guidance:
- Primary ergonomics goals: minimal API surface, idiomatic patterns for mobile/web, ability to opt-out of local proxies per-route.
- JS SDK example:
  const s = client.invokeSpeculative(prompt, {tools:[..], onPartial: (frame) => renderFrame(frame), onReconcile: (frameId, canonical) => handleReplace(frameId, canonical)});
- Provide a small migration helper: specStubRegistry.register('calendar.lookup', jsFn) so teams can gradually onboard.

Observability & safety:
- Telemetry: record speculative-start, speculative-accept, speculative-reject, reconciliation-latency, divergence-flag.
- Cost accounting: speculative local work not billed; only canonical server execution counted. If local stub later proves incorrect and server retriggers additional heavy compute, we surface that as reconciliation re-run cost.
- Safety: speculative stubs flagged non-authoritative. Any frame that could result in side-effects must include serverConfirmationRequired=true; SDK must block final commit until canonical answer is received.

Rollout strategy:
- Phase 0 (internal): ship SDK hooks and server reconciliation frames behind feature flag for partner teams (Q2 beta).
- Phase 1 (curated stubs): enable three curated stubs for mobile product flows (search, contact, math). Validate divergence metrics.
- Phase 2 (opt-in customers): expose stub registry to customers with opt-in contract and audit logs.
- Phase 3 (general availability): default fallback stubs removed; allow customer-managed stubs.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Where to run local stubs? JS only; consider WASM sandbox for iOS/Android portability. Platform cost of shipping stubs and security review?
- How to keep divergence UX understandable for end-users? Suggest a lightweight UI pattern: fade-out replacement with inline "Updated" indicator.
- How to limit complexity of reconciliation patches to minimize server processing and network overhead?

Next steps / immediate action items:
- Tech spike: prototype JS SDK flows + small calendar lookup stub (owner: Marco, 2w).
- Console: add reconciliation telemetry visualization (owner: Lina, 3w).
- Security: run threat model on stub execution and registry (owner: Rory, 1w).
- Draft developer migration guide and sample app for mobile (owner: Ava, 2w).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is exploratory and intentionally leans toward improving UX in low-connectivity contexts. Feedback wanted on acceptable divergence thresholds, billing model edge cases, and policy for customer-supplied stubs.
